newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan life insurers to sell auto, fire cover - paper.
newsitem.headline: Japan life insurers to sell auto, fire cover - paper.

text.p: Japan's four major life insurance companies will start selling auto and fire insurance to large corporations from October through their non-life insurance units, a Japanese newspaper said on Thursday.
The economic daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said the life insurers previously had a self-imposed policy preventing their non-life insurance subsidiaries from selling such cover to corporate customers.
But they decided to change the policy after Japan's Fair Trade Commission conducted hearings on possible monopoly practices, the paper said.
The policy was established as a tentative measure to avoid possible friction in the process of life insurance firms' entrance into the non-life insurance market, the paper said.
The four companies are Nippon Life Insurance Co, Dai-ichi Mutual Insurance Co, Sumitomo Life Insurance Co and Meiji LIfe Insurance Co.
